title: Job Interview
summary: An interviewer asks a candidate about experience, strengths, and why they want the job.
description: A short intermediate-level interview simulation. Useful vocabulary includes 'strengths and weaknesses', 'relevant experience', and 'teamwork'. The interview ends with a polite close.

vocabulary.definition: a person who is being considered for a job
knowledge or skill you get from doing a job
the things you are good at
the ability to work well with other people
able to start doing something, for example a new job

dialogue.text: Good morning. Please, have a seat. So, tell me a little about yourself.
Good morning. My name is Daniel. I have five years of experience in marketing.
Great. What would you say are your main strengths?
I am organised, I work well under pressure, and I enjoy teamwork.
Sometimes I am too detail-oriented, but I am learning to prioritise better.
Why do you want to work for our company?
I admire your focus on sustainability, and I would love to grow in this field.
When would you be available to start?
I can start in two weeks, after giving notice at my current job.
Thank you, Daniel. We will contact you by the end of the week.

questions.q: How many years of experience does Daniel have?
What is one of Daniel's strengths?

trueFalse.statement: Daniel has ten years of marketing experience.
trueFalse.explanation: Daniel says he has five years of experience in marketing.

trueFalse.statement: Daniel admires the company's focus on sustainability.
trueFalse.explanation: Daniel explicitly says 'I admire your focus on sustainability.'

teacherTips: Pre-teach formulaic interview phrases: 'I would say', 'I am good at…', 'My weakness is…'
After listening, students write five bullet points about themselves following the same structure.
Run a mock interview in pairs using the same questions, then swap roles.

es.title: Entrevista de trabajo
es.summary: Un entrevistador pregunta a un candidato sobre su experiencia, sus puntos fuertes y por qué quiere el puesto.
es.description: Una breve simulación de entrevista de nivel intermedio. El vocabulario útil incluye 'strengths and weaknesses', 'relevant experience' y 'teamwork'. La entrevista termina con un cierre educado.

vocabulary.definition: una persona que está siendo considerada para un trabajo
conocimiento o habilidad que obtienes al hacer un trabajo
las cosas en las que eres bueno
la capacidad de trabajar bien con otras personas
capaz de empezar a hacer algo, por ejemplo un trabajo nuevo

questions.q: ¿Cuál es uno de los puntos fuertes de Daniel?

trueFalse.statement: Daniel tiene diez años de experiencia en marketing.
trueFalse.explanation: Daniel dice que tiene cinco años de experiencia en marketing.

trueFalse.statement: Daniel admira el enfoque de sostenibilidad de la empresa.
trueFalse.explanation: Daniel dice explícitamente 'I admire your focus on sustainability'.

teacherTips: Enseña antes fórmulas de entrevista: 'I would say', 'I am good at…', 'My weakness is…'.
Después de escuchar, los estudiantes escriben cinco puntos sobre sí mismos siguiendo la misma estructura.
Haz una entrevista simulada por parejas usando las mismas preguntas y luego intercambiad los papeles.
